title: use justfile for multi-arch build orchestration
description:
## Decision

Use justfile (just command runner) to provide standardized recipes for building, testing, and pushing multi-architecture images.

## Rationale

- Simple, readable task definitions without Makefile complexity.
- Variable-based design (name, namespace, dockerfile, platforms) makes recipes reusable across services with minimal changes.
- Recipes are self-documenting via just --list.
- Supports importing shared recipe files (just import) for future cross-repo reuse.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Makefile**: Verbose syntax, whitespace-sensitive, less readable.
- **Shell scripts**: No dependency/ordering support, harder to discover available tasks.
- **Task (taskfile.dev)**: YAML-based, more overhead for simple recipes.

## Affects

- All local build and push workflows; CI can call just recipes for consistency

title: use docker buildx over Apple container tool for multi-arch builds
description:
## Decision

Use docker buildx exclusively for multi-architecture image builds on all platforms.

## Rationale

Apple's container tool has serious DNS resolution failures during builds — packages cannot be fetched from Alpine APK or Go module proxy. docker buildx works reliably on both macOS and Linux.

## Alternatives Considered

- **apple/container (OS-conditional routing)**: Implemented first but abandoned due to DNS failures blocking apk add and go mod download inside the build.
- **Separate CI-only builds**: Rejected — developers need to build locally to test.

## Affects

- justfile recipes: build-multiarch, build-amd64, build-arm64, push-ghcr

title: apply UPX compression on amd64 only, skip on arm64
description:
## Decision

UPX binary compression is applied conditionally: only when TARGETARCH=amd64.

## Rationale

UPX is not reliable on arm64 — it causes build failures and corrupted binaries in Alpine + QEMU emulation scenarios. amd64 builds benefit from ~60-70% size reduction with no such issues.

## Alternatives Considered

- **UPX on all architectures**: Breaks arm64 builds.
- **No UPX at all**: Larger amd64 image for no benefit.
- **upx --best on arm64 only**: Unreliable; dropped.

## Affects

- Dockerfile.multiarch builder stage RUN steps

title: cross-compile using BUILDPLATFORM/TARGETPLATFORM Docker args
description:
## Decision

Builder stage uses --platform=\$BUILDPLATFORM (native host) and cross-compiles via GOOS/GOARCH targeting \$TARGETOS/\$TARGETARCH.

## Rationale

Building on the native host platform avoids slow QEMU emulation. Go cross-compilation is first-class and does not require emulation. amd64 builds on Apple Silicon are 5-10x faster this way.

## Alternatives Considered

- **QEMU emulation (--platform=\$TARGETPLATFORM for builder)**: Slow, especially for amd64 on arm64 host.
- **Separate native CI runners per arch**: More complex pipeline, not needed given Go's cross-compilation.

## Affects

- Dockerfile.multiarch FROM builder stage
- go build RUN step (CGO_ENABLED=0 required)

title: use Alpine builder and distroless/static runtime in Dockerfile
description:
## Decision

Two-stage Dockerfile: golang:1.25-bookworm as builder, gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12 as runtime.

## Rationale

- Alpine gives apk tooling (upx, etc.) during build with a small footprint.
- distroless/static has no shell, no package manager, minimal attack surface — appropriate for a static Go binary.
- The combination produces a minimal, secure runtime image.

## Alternatives Considered

- **scratch**: No CA certificates or timezone data; painful for services making HTTPS calls.
- **Alpine runtime**: Larger image, shell present (unnecessary attack surface).
- **debian-slim runtime**: Larger, not needed for CGO_ENABLED=0 binary.

## Affects

- Dockerfile.multiarch both stages
